title: An interrupt right after claim installs its SIGTERM handler, before the block that restores it opens, leaves the handler installed
goal: claim restores the SIGTERM handler it replaced on an interrupt that lands right after the handler is installed

run:
import json, os, signal, subprocess, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import backlog
r = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(r), *a], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
g("init", "-q")
(r / "backlog.json").write_text(json.dumps({"item_dir": "items"}))
(r / "items").mkdir()
item = {"id": "ST-aaaaaaaa", "kind": "story", "title": "t", "status": "todo", "priority": "P3", "goal": "g", "touches": ["x.txt"], "checks": [{"run": ["python3", "-c", "pass"]}]}
(r / "items" / "ST-aaaaaaaa.json").write_text(json.dumps(item, indent=2) + "\n")
g("add", "-A")
g("-c", "user.name=x", "-c", "user.email=x@example.com", "commit", "-qm", "i")
def mine(*_):
    pass
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, mine)
real = signal.signal
def interrupt_after_install(num, handler):
    old = real(num, handler)
    if handler is not mine and callable(handler):
        signal.signal = real
        raise KeyboardInterrupt
    return old
signal.signal = interrupt_after_install
os.environ["CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"] = "chk"
os.environ.pop("KB_BACKLOG_CONFIG", None)
try:
    backlog.main(["--root", str(r), "claim", "ST-aaaaaaaa", "--by", "w"])
except BaseException as e:
    print("claim ended with", type(e).__name__)
finally:
    signal.signal = real
restored = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) is mine
print("SIGTERM handler restored after an interrupt right after claim installed it:", restored)
sys.exit(0 if restored else 1)
